titleStmt.title: Kephalaia of the Teacher, edition page 70: diplomatic and Leiden transcription

sourceDesc.bibl: Kephalaia (Manichäische Handschriften der Staatlichen Museen Berlin), ed. H. J. Polotsky and A. Böhlig, Stuttgart: Kohlhammer, 70. Restorations, sublinear dots, gap counts and corrections are the editors'.

encodingDesc.p: EpiDoc. Read by eye from the page image; gap counts, sublinear dots and supralinear stroke extents verified by measurement on the image. A supralinear stroke is marked on every letter it covers by at least half its width. Spaces are the edition's word division. Facsimile zones are measured line centres. The editors' German statements are not transcribed: each is mapped to an id of the controlled vocabulary data/kephalaia/editorial_vocabulary.json and carried as @ana (ed: statements in the text, app: apparatus footnotes, tr: categories of the transcriber's commentary).

div.p: The framed manuscript page number [ⲟ] (top left, even page) is restored in brackets; the bars above and below are the frame (no strokes). The running title [ⲛⲕⲉⲫⲁⲗⲁⲓⲟⲛ] is restored in brackets, with a stroke over its ⲛ. Every dot run was counted from the `dots` x-positions (runs of 10 or more from the positions only).

Reconcile flags explained by position: dots at the zone centre (tops less than 2 px below it) on ll. 10, 11, 12 (552–632), 16 (554–870), 18 (606), 20 (553, 580), 21 (555–712); dots of area < 6 on ll. 3 (819) and 5 (581); l. 2 counts the margin numeral (470); l. 14 counts the dot under the restored ⲟ (770), a dotted letter inside a restoration (30.18).
Lines 1–7 are not in `bands` (rows of dots); their y-values come from the dots and the margin numerals (§3.24). Line 1 is 26 illegible dots (553–1213).

Lines 2–5 begin with a run of dots closed by a bracket that has no opener on the line and none at the end of p. 069 → ‡ after the letters or dots before it (60.2–12); the dots are illegible; ⲕⲓ (2) and ϩⲟⲩ (5) look restored and are encoded as read (29.28).
Twenty illegible dots (553–1055) before ⲕⲓ]ⲛⲇⲩⲛⲟⲥ; ⲇ in its triangle form.
Twenty illegible dots (553–1055), then the bracket; three illegible dots after ⲙⲡⲕⲁϩ (1324–1376).
Nineteen illegible dots (553–1028); dot under ⲛ after the bracket (1050). Measured stroke over ⲙⲛ (1090–1109, row 463): ⲙ (1080–1099) 50 %, ⲛ (1102–1115) 57 %; both.
Nineteen illegible dots (553–1030); diaeresis over ⲓ of ]ⲓⲧⲉ (1114, 1119) and a dot joined under it (1116, the "!" shape, 43.17); ⲉⲙⲛ without stroke; ϣ of ϣⲓ undotted.
The whole line is 28 illegible dots (553–1263).
"leer" after nine illegible dots (553–764) → vac. Kephalaion 23 ends here, with no end sign.

Chapter opening: the numeral [ⲕⲇ] (24) stands centred in brackets between the margin numerals 8 and 9 and is attached to l. 8 (30.14). It has a bar above (919–952 and 955–982, rows 636–639; ⲕ 100 %, ⲇ 69 %) and a second bar below; the upper bar is encoded as the numeral's stroke, as on every chapter numeral, the lower bar is a frame line and is not encoded (decided here).
Line 9 has no text: its numeral stands beside the space taken by the centred chapter numeral. Encoded as a blank line (vac.), which the editors do not mark with "leer" (decided here).

The title follows in ll. 10–11, two lines of ten illegible dots each (827–1064). The margin numerals [ⲕⲇ] stand level with l. 10: the left one (733–793) with a bar above (731–794, row 708) and a frame bar below, encoded like the centred numeral; the right one (1140–1200) without any bar.
A closing bracket after ten dots (796–802) with no opener on the line → ‡.
Ten illegible dots (552–789), fifteen (825–1195); dots under ⲟ (1229) and ϭ (1297) of ⲟⲩⲛⲁϭ; stroke over ⲛ of ⲛⲕⲣ[ⲓ] (1330–1343).

"[ⲧⲏⲥ . . . . . ⲟⲩⲭⲣⲟ[ⲛⲟⲥ]": the first bracket is not closed before a second opening bracket; restored letters and dots are one restoration, closed after the last dot, and ⲟⲩⲭⲣⲟ is extant (45.26, 35.31; decided here for this form).
Five dots in the first restoration (622–728); ⲭ in ⲟⲩⲭⲣⲟ[ⲛⲟⲥ]; dots under ⲟ, ⲩ of ⲟⲩⲛ (917, 931); one illegible dot (1076), five in the bracket (1112–1218).
"[ⲫⲉ . . . . . ⲁϥⲟ̣ⲩⲱ]ⲛϩ̀": restored letters, dots and further letters in one bracket pair, one restoration with a dotted restored ⲟ (58.14, 30.18).
